events.reason: Left leg swelling and pain after long flight

conditions.label: Acute embolism and thrombosis of left popliteal vein

reports.text:
VENOUS DUPLEX ULTRASOUND, LEFT LOWER EXTREMITY
Indication: Left calf swelling, redness and pain after prolonged air travel.
Technique: Grayscale compression, color and spectral Doppler of the left common femoral, femoral, popliteal and calf veins; right common femoral vein for comparison.
Findings: The left popliteal vein is noncompressible and distended with echogenic intraluminal thrombus and no color flow, consistent with occlusive thrombus. The left common femoral and femoral veins are fully compressible with normal phasic flow. Visualized posterior tibial and peroneal veins compress normally. Right common femoral vein compressible with normal respiratory phasicity. No Baker cyst.
reports.conclusion: Occlusive acute deep vein thrombosis of the left popliteal vein.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 10/11/2025.
Allergies: NKDA.

CC: L lower leg swelling and pain.

HPI: 72 y/o M with COPD, HTN, CAD, CKD 3a, and influenza this past April, here with two days of left calf swelling, redness and an aching pain that came on gradually. Symptoms started after he got home from a 14-hour international flight on which he was seated most of the time. No chest pain, no new dyspnea, no hemoptysis. No prior clots. No recent surgery.

Meds: lisinopril, metoprolol, aspirin, atorvastatin per pt.
Home med list on file: metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily, albuterol 90 mcg q4-6h prn wheezing.

SH: former smoker, 25 pack-years. Social alcohol.

Exam: T 37.1 C (98.8 F), BP 132/78, P 84, RR 16. Comfortable. Left calf visibly swollen and red, mildly warm, tender along the back of the calf; Homans positive. Right leg normal. DP/PT pulses intact both sides. Skin intact, no ulcers. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear.

Data: CBC, BMP and PT/INR unremarkable, creatinine at his known CKD baseline. Venous duplex: occlusive thrombus in the left popliteal vein.

MDM: Acute proximal DVT, L popliteal, provoked by long-haul travel. Hemodynamically stable, no PE symptoms. Renal function adequate for weight-based LMWH. Discussed heparin drip vs LMWH with medicine; stable and able to take SC injections, so LMWH. Given age, comorbidities and limited mobility at home, admitted to medicine for initiation.

Dispo: admit, hospital medicine. Enoxaparin first dose given in ED.

medications.reason: Acute DVT, left popliteal vein; planned 3 months

reports.text:
PORTABLE CHEST, SINGLE AP VIEW
Indication: New fever and productive cough, hospitalized patient.
Comparison: None available.
Findings: Patchy airspace opacity in the right lower lobe. No pleural effusion. No pneumothorax. Cardiomediastinal silhouette within normal limits for technique. Lines/tubes: none.
reports.conclusion: Right lower lobe infiltrate, consistent with pneumonia in the appropriate clinical setting.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital, Medicine service.
Admitted 10/11/2025. Discharged 10/20/2025 to short-term rehabilitation.
Allergies: NKDA.

Principal diagnosis: Acute DVT, left popliteal vein, provoked (prolonged air travel).
Secondary: Hospital-onset pneumonia, right lower lobe. COPD. HTN. CAD, stable. CKD stage 3a.

Hospital course:
1. L popliteal DVT. Admitted from ED after duplex showed occlusive popliteal thrombus. Weight 82 kg, CrCl above 30, so enoxaparin 80 mg SC q12h. Leg pain and swelling improved steadily. No signs of PE. After 9 days of enoxaparin, transitioned to apixaban 5 mg BID on day of discharge. Planned duration 3 months given a clear transient provoking factor; PCP to decide on stopping. Aspirin 81 continued for CAD; bleeding precautions reviewed.
2. Pneumonia. On hospital day 3 (10/14) new temp 38.4 C and a productive cough. WBC 13.8. Portable CXR with RLL infiltrate. Started cefepime 2 g IV q12h, 7-day course through 10/20. Needed 2 L nasal cannula for about two days, weaned to room air by 10/17. Never required higher support or ICU. Afebrile since 10/16.
3. Deconditioning. Weak after the pneumonia; PT evaluated and recommended short-term rehab before home, where he lives alone. Pt agreed.
4. COPD, HTN, CAD, CKD: home regimen continued. Creatinine stable at baseline.

Discharge medications:
- apixaban 5 mg PO BID (NEW)
- lisinopril 20 mg daily
- metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily
- aspirin 81 mg daily
- atorvastatin 40 mg qhs
- tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily
- albuterol HFA 1-2 puffs q4-6h prn
Cefepime completed 10/20.

Follow-up: PCP within 1-2 weeks of rehab discharge, re: anticoagulation duration.

documents.title: Patient Call From Hospital
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called from his hospital room to let PCP know he was admitted Saturday with a blood clot in his left leg after his flight home. On blood thinner shots, leg already feels a little better. ED record received this am and routed. Told him we'll watch for the discharge paperwork and to call when he's out.

documents.title: Rehab Facility Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Nurse from the short-term rehab facility called to confirm med list for pt admitted there 10/20. Reviewed against hospital d/c summary: apixaban 5 BID, lisinopril 20, metoprolol succ 50, ASA 81, atorva 40 qhs, tiotropium daily, albuterol prn. Antibiotic finished in hospital 10/20. Confirmed ASA continues with apixaban per hospital team. She reports he is working with PT twice a day, walking the hallway with a walker. Expected stay 2-3 weeks. Asked them to send their summary at discharge.

documents.title: Rehabilitation Facility Discharge Summary
documents.author: rehabilitation
documents.body:
Short-term rehabilitation discharge summary.
Admit 10/20/2025, discharge 11/07/2025 to home.
Allergies: NKDA.

Reason for stay: deconditioning after hospitalization for left popliteal DVT complicated by pneumonia.

Course: Participated in PT/OT daily. Progressed from rolling walker to independent ambulation on level surfaces and one flight of stairs with rail. Independent in ADLs at discharge. Lungs clear by end of stay, on room air throughout. Left leg swelling much improved. Apixaban taken without bleeding.

Discharge meds: apixaban 5 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg qhs, tiotropium 18 mcg daily, albuterol prn.

Home exercise program provided. No home services needed per pt. PCP follow-up to be arranged by patient.

documents.title: Post-Rehab Scheduling
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called pt after rehab summary came in. He got home Friday, says he's glad to be in his own bed. Booked f/u with PCP 11/18 at 10:30.

documents.title: Diarrhea
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pt called: watery diarrhea since Tues, lots of it, "going all day," maybe 8-10 times. No blood that he's seen. Crampy belly. Feels weak and lightheaded getting up. Drinking but can't keep up. No fever that he's checked.

Recent IV antibiotics in hospital last month + rehab stay, on apixaban, CKD. Concerned for C. diff and dehydration. Discussed with PCP: needs evaluation tonight - ED for stool testing, labs and fluids. Pt reluctant to go on a Friday night, says he'll go first thing if it doesn't settle. Advised strongly to go sooner if dizzy, any blood, fever, or making little urine. He verbalized understanding.

conditions.label: Enterocolitis due to Clostridioides difficile, not specified as recurrent

reports.text:
ABDOMEN, SUPINE AND UPRIGHT
Indication: Severe diarrhea, evaluate for colonic dilatation.
Findings: Nonobstructive bowel gas pattern. No colonic dilatation; transverse colon caliber within normal limits. No free intraperitoneal air. No pneumatosis. Osseous structures unremarkable for age.
reports.conclusion: No colonic dilatation. No evidence of toxic megacolon.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 11/15/2025.
Allergies: NKDA.

CC: diarrhea.

HPI: 72-year-old man with COPD, HTN, CAD and CKD stage 3a, treated for a left popliteal DVT about a month ago (that admission complicated by pneumonia treated with IV antibiotics), then a short rehab stay. Since shortly after getting home from rehab 11/7 he has had profuse watery diarrhea, onset 11/11, many episodes daily, crampy lower abdominal pain, weakness and lightheadedness on standing. No hematochezia. No vomiting.

Home meds (as entered at triage): lisinopril 20 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg qhs, tiotropium 18 mcg inh daily, albuterol 90 mcg prn.

SH: former smoker, 25 pk-yr, quit about 8 yrs ago. Social drinker. Retired postal worker.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Tired, dry mucous membranes. Abdomen soft, mildly tender throughout, not distended, bowel sounds active, no rebound or guarding. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Left calf without significant swelling.

Data: WBC 17.2. Creatinine 1.72 (baseline about 1.5). Stool C. difficile toxin positive. Abdominal films: no colonic dilatation.

MDM: C. difficile infection, severe by leukocytosis, after recent antibiotic exposure. No ileus, no megacolon, hemodynamically stable. IV fluids started. Oral vancomycin 125 mg QID started in ED. Lisinopril held given volume depletion. Contact precautions.

Dispo: admit to medicine.

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth four times daily for 10 days (started 11/15)

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital, Medicine service.
Admitted 11/15/2025. Discharged 11/19/2025 to home.
Allergies: NKDA.

Principal diagnosis: Severe Clostridioides difficile infection, initial episode, without toxic megacolon.
Other: recent L popliteal DVT on apixaban; recent pneumonia; COPD; HTN; CAD; CKD 3a.

Course: Presented with profuse watery diarrhea after recent IV antibiotics. WBC 17.2, creatinine 1.72 on arrival; stool toxin positive; abdominal films without colonic dilatation. Treated with oral vancomycin 125 mg QID (day 1 = 11/15) and IV fluids. Stool frequency fell from double digits to 2-3 soft stools daily by 11/18, cramping resolved, tolerating diet. WBC 10.9 and creatinine 1.58 on the morning of discharge. Lisinopril held on admission for volume depletion; resumed at discharge as he is eating and drinking well and creatinine is near baseline. Apixaban continued throughout. No new antibiotics.

Discharge medications:
- vancomycin 125 mg PO QID - continue through 11/24 to complete 10 days
- apixaban 5 mg PO BID
- lisinopril 20 mg daily (resume)
- metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily
- aspirin 81 mg daily
- atorvastatin 40 mg qhs
- tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily
- albuterol HFA prn

Instructions: wash hands with soap and water; bleach-based cleaning of bathroom. Return for recurrent diarrhea, fever, abdominal swelling or pain. PCP follow-up within one week with BMP and CBC.

documents.title: Transitional Care Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: TCM call, discharged yesterday. Pt home, says he feels "wrung out but human." Two soft BMs since getting home, no watery stool. No fever. Eating small meals, drinking water and broth. Has vancomycin caps, taking 4x/day, last dose 11/24. Taking apixaban BID. Restarted lisinopril today per d/c instructions. Reviewed handwashing with soap (sanitizer doesn't kill the spores), bleach wipes for the bathroom. Missed 11/18 appt while inpatient; PCP visit booked Mon 11/24 with labs. Reviewed when to call.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital f/u. Rough fall: L popliteal DVT 10/11 after flight home from abroad, admitted, enoxaparin -> apixaban, pneumonia in hospital treated with cefepime, rehab 10/20-11/7. Then C. diff 11/11, admitted 11/15-11/19 on oral vanc. Both discharge summaries and ED records reviewed.

Today: stools formed, once or twice a day, since about Friday. No cramping, no fever. Appetite coming back. Last vanc doses today. Leg: swelling basically gone, occasional ache in the calf at end of day. Breathing at his baseline, no cough. No bleeding on apixaban - no black stools, no blood in urine, gums ok.

Meds reconciled: apixaban 5 BID, vancomycin 125 QID through today, lisinopril 20 (back on since 11/20), metoprolol succ 50, ASA 81, atorva 40, tiotropium, albuterol prn.

Exam: vitals as charted. Down ~4 kg since summer. Looks tired but much better than he sounded on the phone. Lungs clear, no crackles at the R base. Heart RRR. Abd soft, NT, ND, normal BS. L calf soft, nontender, no meaningful asymmetry. No edema.

A/P
1. C. diff, severe, initial episode - clinically resolving, completing vanc today. Reviewed recurrence signs; call right away with watery diarrhea. Avoid unneeded antibiotics going forward.
2. L popliteal DVT, provoked - apixaban 5 BID. Plan 3 months total -> mid-January. Continue ASA per hospital; will revisit when apixaban stops.
3. Pneumonia - treated, lungs clear. Resolved.
4. CKD 3a - BMP today. Back on lisinopril.
5. Weight loss from illness - expect it back as he eats.
RTC mid-Jan.
